newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB ends down after denial by MOF's Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB ends down after denial by MOF's Sakakibara.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session easier after a denial by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of Ministry of Finance's (MOF) International Finance Bureau, that he had said Japan was not likely to raise interest rates until the end of March, 1997.
Earlier, a Japanese news agency quoted Sakakibara as telling a U.S. economist that Japan would not raise interest rates at least until the end of the current fiscal year ending March 31.
December ended at 122.15, down from Monday's 122.20.
The denial temporarily pushed the December contract down to 122.04, but it crawled up a little by the end of the day.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.815 percent, unchanged from Monday.
The MOF's tender of 500 billion yen worth of 1.7 percent four-year notes produced an average price of 100.14 and lowest price of 100.11.

Four major Japanese brokerages were estimated to have bought the largest part, or 370 billion yen, of the offer, traders said. Life insurers also appeared to have bought the new notes for their portfolio, they said.
Meanwhile, city banks have been buying call options of the recently issued 10-year JGBs in a bid to hedge against risks involved in a further market advance, traders said.
Banks remain interested in getting profits out of spread trading between short- and long-term instruments, traders said.
This is done by raising funds in the short end of the market and investing them in the long end, taking advantage of the positive yield curve, they said.
Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Saturday that he sees the Bank of Japan keeping an easy monetary stance for now. -- Yoshiko Mori, Tokyo Treasury Desk 813-3432-8676
